newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesia's Suharto urges rich to help poor.
newsitem.headline: Indonesia's Suharto urges rich to help poor.

text.p: Indonesian President Suharto urged wealthy businessmen on Saturday to help the poor and avoid the poverty gap being used as a political issue.
"We must reduce things that can be used as political issues, such as the poverty gap and others," Suharto told about 300 businessmen at the Bogor palace, some 60 km (37 miles) south of Jakarta.
Indonesia estimates about 26 million of its more than 195 million citizens live below the official poverty line.
Suharto said political stability was important for the country's continued development and warned that some groups in society were trying to change the political laws.
"Without stability, national development will not be reached," he said.
"There are people that want to revoke political laws but they have a lack of understanding about the constitution."
Suharto cited riots in Jakarta on July 27, the worst in the capital in more than 20 years, as an example of this lack of understanding.
"Like or not, we must face all (such problems) with firm action. It is only a small group and it was not rooted in the people. They misused the openness and freedom that we developed," he said.
The government has blamed the the small left-wing People's Democratic Party (PRD), which it says employs the tactics of the banned Indonesian Communist Party (PKI), for being behind the riots.
Most of the group's leaders are now in detention facing subversion charges, which carry a maximum penalty of death.
The official human rights commission says five people died and 74 were reported missing as a result of the riots.
